title: Repository Scale — Source to Ground
purpose: A neutral navigation scale for the archive. It describes how concretely a record is expressed, from source/orientation through structures and actors to events, records and the smallest material traces.
principle: Scale is not importance, truth, value or power. It is granularity. Domain, time, epistemic status and graph relationships remain independent coordinates.

axis.label: Source
axis.question: What gives the system its originating direction or premise?

axis.label: Principles
axis.question: What rules, values or ideas organize what follows?

axis.label: Concepts & Patterns
axis.question: What recurring ideas, symbols, classifications or patterns are being formed?

axis.label: Worlds & Domains
axis.question: What broad field or environment does the subject inhabit?

axis.label: Regions & Territories
axis.question: Where is the field divided geographically or jurisdictionally?

axis.label: Institutions & Structures
axis.question: What durable structures coordinate people, resources or authority?

axis.label: Networks & Groups
axis.question: What collections of actors are connected through relationships?

axis.label: People & Living Actors
axis.question: Who or what living actors participate?

axis.label: Bodies & Objects
axis.question: What embodied or material things carry the system?

axis.label: Events & Actions
axis.question: What happens, changes, moves or is done?

axis.label: Records & Signals
axis.question: What trace lets us observe, remember or communicate what happened?

axis.label: Ground / Grain / Dust
axis.question: What is the smallest concrete or material trace relevant to this investigation?

placement_rules: Place each record at its most useful primary scale, not at every scale it touches.
Use explicit scale overrides for canonical records where automatic inference would be misleading.
Keep domains separate from scale: religion, politics, economy, science, geography and Potatoism can occur at any scale.
Keep time separate from scale: a source can be ancient, a current institution can have a long history, and a record can describe the future.
Keep epistemic status separate from scale: mythic canon, project theory, historical record and observable evidence can all exist at any scale.
A graph edge can cross any number of scale levels. The tree is a reading route, not a claim that reality is strictly hierarchical.
